info.name: BlockEvidence API
info.description:
K2. Mirrors the live Spring controllers exactly - every endpoint through Phase 5 (F2/F3 encryption, F5 retry, I1 report, plus every Phase 1-4 endpoint), not just Phase 1-2. Run the Auth folder first (top to bottom) to populate the token variables every other request depends on, then Cases, then Evidence/Custody in order - later requests in those folders depend on ids/versions set by earlier ones in the SAME run (expectedVersion in particular: each write bumps the ledger version, so requests must run in the order they appear, not out of order or twice).

See docs/features/k2-api-documentation.md for the full account and live verification log, and /swagger-ui.html on a running instance for the generated OpenAPI docs (same source of truth: the controller annotations).

item.name: Evidence
item.description: B1-B5, C2, C3, F2/F3, I1. The core resource.

request.description: Role: COLLECTOR or FORENSIC_ANALYST. Multipart: JSON part "metadata" + binary part "file" - ships pre-attached to postman/sample-evidence.txt (relative to this collection's own folder) so the request runs unattended via Newman; swap in any real file in the Postman UI instead. F2/F3 (automatic): the file and metadata are AES-256-GCM encrypted before being pinned to IPFS; the ledger's recorded hash covers the ciphertext. Run Create case first so {{caseNumber}} is set.

formdata.value: {"caseId": "{{caseNumber}}", "type": "DIGITAL", "description": "Postman collection demo - seized phone image", "location": "Evidence locker 4"}

exec: pm.test('file is encrypted: fileSha256 present on the ledger record', () => pm.expect(body.fileSha256).to.be.a('string'));

request.description: Role: COLLECTOR or FORENSIC_ANALYST. PHYSICAL evidence must NOT include a file part.
Any authenticated role (H1). Served from the G3 read model.
Any authenticated role. metadata is decrypted with the CALLER's own wrapped content key.
Re-fetches and re-hashes stored content against the ledger (C2); audited as a DOWNLOAD.
Any authenticated role. {{fileCid}} was captured by Register DIGITAL evidence's own test script above - every evidence item that ever referenced this CID comes back.
Any authenticated role (B4). Every earlier version stays readable.
Any authenticated role (C3). Every committed version with its real Fabric transaction id.
Deliberately run AS THE JUDGE, who may hold no content key for this item at all: verify() needs none (F2/F3 design) - only IPFS reachability. Proves the property live.

I1 - also run AS THE JUDGE deliberately, for the same reason as Verify above: the report is built entirely from ledger + verification data, never decrypted content, so a Judge with no content key still gets the full report. Response body is the PDF bytes.

F2 Q3. The ONE read that needs content access - the caller's wrapped key decrypts the file. Try this same request with {{judgeToken}} instead (a role never wrapped in for this item) to see 403 KEY_NOT_AUTHORISED.
Role: COLLECTOR or FORENSIC_ANALYST, AND must hold a wrapped content key for this item (F2/F3 side effect). expectedVersion is optimistic concurrency - match the item's current version exactly.
Role: COLLECTOR or PROSECUTOR (B5, step 1 of 2). Nothing is removed yet.
Role: JUDGE only (step 2 of 2). Status becomes DISPOSED; the record is never deleted (C-02) - still readable and verifiable forever.

Role: JUDGE only. Deliberately run AFTER Approve above to demonstrate the two are mutually exclusive on the same version - Approve already moved the item to version 4, so this one's expectedVersion=3 is now stale. A genuine 409 VERSION_CONFLICT here is the CORRECT, asserted outcome, not a broken request.

exec: pm.test('409 Conflict (EXPECTED - Approve above already consumed this version)', () => pm.response.to.have.status(409));

item.name: Custody & Status
item.description: D1-D3. Status state machine and two-step custody transfer.

request.description: A fresh item just for this folder, so its own version sequence (below) never collides with whatever the Evidence folder already did to {{evidenceId}}. Run Create case first.
Role: COLLECTOR, FORENSIC_ANALYST or PROSECUTOR (D1). Must follow the legal state machine in order - a skip is 409 INVALID_STATE.
Role: any custody-capable role, and must be the CURRENT CUSTODIAN (D2, step 1 of 2). Custody does NOT move yet. Needs {{analystId}} - run Me as the analyst once beforehand.
Must be the NAMED RECEIVER (step 2 of 2). The only step that actually moves custody.
Role: any custody-capable role. Only the caller's own pending transfers as receiver.
Any authenticated role (D3). Custody-relevant events only, from the ledger's full history.
Any authenticated role (H3). Newest first, from G3's off-chain read model.
Any authenticated role (H2). Aggregate counts only.
Any authenticated role (H4). Always the caller's own - the analyst should see a TRANSFER_PENDING notification here after Initiate custody transfer above.
Role: ADMIN or AUDITOR only (A6). Every VIEW/DOWNLOAD and failed-auth/denied attempt.
